**Make curiosity and rigorous truth-seeking the default human operating system—stronger than tribal loyalty, ideology, comfort, or fear.**

Not “more education” in the credential sense, and not “be nicer.” I mean rewiring the cultural and individual incentives so that the highest-status, most rewarding thing a person can do is to notice when they’re wrong, update hard on evidence, and keep asking “what’s actually true?” even when it costs them status, friends, or a tidy story.

Why that one lever?

- Almost every persistent catastrophe—poverty traps that refuse better tech, wars that outlast any rational interest, preventable disease, resource fights, and the slow-motion risks of unaligned tech or closed-mindedness—gets worse when people treat preferred narratives as more real than reality. Truth-seeking compounds: better models → better decisions → better tools → more capacity to solve the next hard problem.
- The universe is indifferent and vast. Understanding it (physics, biology, intelligence, the long-term future of consciousness) is both the most interesting project and the only reliable way to not get wiped out by something we failed to model. Curiosity is the engine; truth-seeking is the steering.
- Everything else I might wish for (multiplanetary life, abundant energy, ending unnecessary suffering, longer healthy lifespans, freer exploration) becomes dramatically more achievable once people stop systematically lying to themselves and each other for short-term tribal points.

I wouldn’t impose it by force or some mind-control hack; that just creates new dogmas. I’d want the cultural immune system upgraded so that motivated reasoning feels as embarrassing as basic arithmetic errors, and genuine insight feels as rewarding as it actually is. Humor helps here—ridicule of sacred cows and self-importance is a feature, not a bug.

That’s the change. The rest of the interesting future follows more reliably from it than from any single gadget, law, or redistribution scheme. The cosmos is still mostly unexplored; I’d rather we show up ready to learn than still arguing about whose feelings the data is allowed to hurt.
